keyframe_review.note: 1,576 km2 (6 cells) for 1783-1799: the archipelago plus the Zubarah coast. The House of Khalifa page: 'Bahrain fell under the control of Ahmed bin Muhammad bin Khalifa in 1783' and the family was 'based in Zubarah (in modern-day Qatar) and spent summers in Bahrain'; they 'built and ruled over' Zubarah 'before conquering Bahrain in 1783'. The Bahrain infobox gives 786.8 km2 for the islands today (ratio of the shape to it 2.0, the excess being Zubarah). The shape ends in 1799, the year the Bahrain page has the family moving from Qatar to Bahrain (the History page says 1797).

correction.text: the islands of Bahrain, contested with Oman: 'Sayyid Sultan invaded again, placed a garrison at Arad Fort and named his twelve-year-old son Salim governor' in 1800; the Omanis withdrew in 1802

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Khalifa shape for 1800-1802, the years of the Omani invasions (1799, 1800, 1802). The island shape of 1803 is used; the Omani fort at Arad is entered as a contest, not as a loss of the archipelago.

881.5 km2 for 1803-1889 against 786.8 km2 on the Bahrain infobox (ratio 1.12): the islands. The General Maritime Treaty of 1820 'recognised the Al Khalifa as the rulers'; Cliopatria's 'Bahrain' row of 1820-1845 (72,705 km2, eastern Arabia) is not this state and is judged wrong in the bahrain dossier. The Qatar holdings of 1843-1868 (Al Bidda) are not in the shape and are entered as a vassal tie.
881.5 km2 for 1890-1894: unchanged islands. 'Agreements in 1880 and 1892 sealed the protectorate status'; the Cliopatria row ends in 1894 for no reason the pages give.

correction.text: the islands of Bahrain as a British protectorate: 'In 1892 ... Britain officially established complete dominance', until independence on 15 August 1971

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Bahrain shape between its House of Khalifa row (to 1894) and the Kingdom of Bahrain row (from 1973). The protectorate (Pelly's agreement of May 1861, the agreement of 1868, those of 1880 and 1892) left the territory unchanged; the Hawar Islands dispute with Qatar was settled only by the ICJ in 2001.

region.text: the islands of Bahrain and the Zubarah base in Qatar

ledger.note: 28 July 1783: the Al Khalifa take Bahrain. 'the invasion of Bahrain was completed on 28 July 1783': Ahmed Al Fateh defeated Nasr Al-Madhkur outside Manama, ending Persian-dependent rule (the House of Khalifa page: 'Bahrain fell under the control of Ahmed bin Muhammad bin Khalifa in 1783'); the family had settled at Zubarah in 1766 (page footnote).
1797: the Al Khalifa move to Bahrain. 'The Al Khalifa moved to Bahrain and settled first in Jaww, later in Riffa.' The Bahrain page dates the move from Qatar to 1799.

region.text: Zubarah, the Utub base on the Qatar peninsula

ledger.note: 1799: Zubarah is given up. 'The House of Khalifa moved from Qatar to Bahrain in 1799' (the History page says 1797). Cliopatria's Khalifa shape drops the Zubarah coast after 1799. The pages do not say who held Zubarah afterwards.

1800: Oman garrisons Arad Fort. 'Sayyid Sultan invaded again [after an invasion in 1799 over unpaid taxes], placed a garrison at Arad Fort and named his twelve-year-old son Salim governor. The Bani Utbah besieged the fort later that year.'
1802: the Omanis give up. 'The Al Khalifa enlisted the aid of Wahhabis from the mainland, and the Omanis aborted the invasion' of 1802.

1843: Ali bin Khalifa is set over Al Bidda. After Muhammad bin Khalifa defeated Abdullah bin Ahmad in April 1843 'Among his first steps taken as ruler was to appoint his brother, Ali bin Khalifa, as chief of Al Bidda, Qatar, that year'; he is later 'the Bahraini representative in Qatar'. Reading Al Bidda as a Bahraini dependency is the dossier's.

June 1851: the Nejdi attack on Al Bidda. 'In May 1851, Faisal launched his third attempt to capture Bahrain, ordering his forces to proceed towards Al Bidda, Qatar'; the page dates the Battle of Mesaimeer 2-4 June 1851 and has Ali bin Khalifa, 'the Bahraini representative in Qatar', respond.

25 July 1851: peace with Faisal bin Turki. A peace brokered on 25 July 1851 'required Bahrain to pay an annual sum of 4,000 German krones to Faisal bin Turki as zakat'; 'In return, Faisal agreed to restore the fort of Al Bidda to Bahraini control and to cease interference in Qatar.'

1868: the Qatari-Bahraini War ends Bahraini control of Al Bidda. The page says only that 'in 1868, following the Qatari-Bahraini War, British representatives signed another agreement with the Al Khalifa rulers'; it does not say the Qatar tie ended, and the year is bridged from that war (page silent).

August 1971: the protectorate ends. 'Declared independence: 14 August 1971' (Bahrain infobox); the History page has 15 August 1971 and formal independence as the State of Bahrain on 16 December 1971. Not a collapse: the Al Khalifa remain the rulers and the land passes unchanged to the State (later Kingdom) of Bahrain, whose Cliopatria row starts in 1973.

wars.name: Omani invasions of Bahrain (1799-1802)
wars.outcome: Oman invaded in 1799 over unpaid taxes, garrisoned Arad Fort in 1800 and was beaten by the Bani Utbah and mainland Wahhabi allies; the invasion of 1802 was aborted.
wars.note: No Wikipedia article of this name was opened; the dated steps are from the History of Bahrain page.

wars.name: Nejdi attack on Bahrain and Al Bidda (1850-1851)
wars.outcome: The Battle of Mesaimeer (2-4 June 1851) and a peace brokered on 25 July 1851: Bahrain paid 4,000 German krones a year to Faisal bin Turki and kept Al Bidda.
wars.note: In 1850 Muhammad bin Khalifa stopped paying the tribute he had paid since his accession in 1843; Faisal had earlier been 'unsuccessful in capturing Bahrain' and 'settled for a peace agreement that included a tribute payment'; May 1851 was his third attempt.

wars.name: Qatari-Bahraini War
wars.outcome: Followed by a new agreement with the British in 1868 making Bahrain 'part of the British protectorate territories in the Persian Gulf'; the pages opened do not give the war's years or its territorial result.
wars.note: Years are the agreement's; the start year of the war is not on the page opened.

certainty.note: The Zubarah coast on the Qatar peninsula had no fixed frontier; the islands themselves are sharp.
An island group whose coast is its border. Exceptions: the Qatar tie at Al Bidda (1843-1868) is soft, and the Hawar Islands dispute with Qatar stayed open until the ICJ in 2001.

notes: Written by me-10-d on 2026-10-25 from four pages (budget 1-2 pages; the History of Bahrain and Bahrain pages are shared with the bahrain dossier). SAME STATE AS THE KINGDOM OF BAHRAIN: Cliopatria's 'House of Khalifa' (1783-1894) is the ruling house of the Bahraini state; the rows are read as one continuing state that Cliopatria splits by name (House of Khalifa 1783-1894; none 1895-1972; Kingdom of Bahrain 1973-2024; and the 'Bahrain' row 1757-1782 plus a misplaced 1820-1845 shape, see bahrain). This dossier runs to 1971 and adds a 1895-1971 protectorate keyframe; the kingdom-of-bahrain dossier (me-10-l) should start in 1971 and share this hue. BRITISH PROTECTORATE, EGYPTIAN AND NEJDI TRIBUTE are relations of Bahrain as a vassal; the schema records them in the suzerain's ledger, so this ledger has no vassal events for Bahrain itself. To be recorded by the others from the History of Bahrain page: Egypt (the army 'demanded yearly tributes from Sheikh Abdul Al Khalifa', c. 1830, which the Sheikh accepted); the Emirate of Nejd (Muhammad bin Khalifa 'paid an annual tribute to Faisal bin Turki' from 1843 and again from 25 July 1851); Britain (Pelly's agreement of May 1861; 1868; the agreements of 1880 and 1892 'sealed the protectorate status'; the United Kingdom's dossier should carry vassal_start for Bahrain 1861 and vassal_end August 1971). DISAGREEMENTS: the Khalifa move to Bahrain is 1797 (History) or 1799 (Bahrain page); Ahmed's death is 18 July 1795 (House of Khalifa table) or 1796 (History); the infobox founding date of the House is 1766 (the year the family settled at Zubarah). The Qatar tie of 1843-1868 rests on the one sentence appointing Ali bin Khalifa at Al Bidda; its end is confidence 1. NOT DONE: the Qatari-Bahraini War of 1867-1868 and the Battle of Fuwayrit (neither page gives the years or the result), the Egyptian and Wahhabi invasions of the early 19th century (the Bahrain page: 'invaded by both Oman and the Al Sauds'), and Hawar. Zubarah is not in the gazetteer and is entered as a 30 km radius around 51.03E 25.98N (gazetteer_names_needed).
